hero.headline: Oil prices climb as U.S. and Iran exchange military strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices rose after the United States and Iran conducted a fresh exchange of military strikes, adding volatility to global energy markets as investors assessed both the immediate military risk and ongoing diplomatic efforts.

The U.S. military struck an Iranian military facility, targeting a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch attack drones. American forces shot down four Iranian drones near the Strait of Hormuz. A U.S. official characterized the action as "measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire."

Within two hours, Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched retaliatory strikes against an American military base in Kuwait. Kuwait's army confirmed it intercepted hostile missile and drone threats early Thursday morning. The Iranian state broadcaster reported the strikes targeted the base that had served as the source of the U.S. attack.

The tit-for-tat strikes coincided with Iranian forces firing at four ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. An Iranian official stated the vessels had crossed without coordination with security forces.

The military escalation underscores how fragile negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain. While both sides have maintained diplomatic channels, President Trump delivered harsh rhetoric aimed at forcing a deal. "Either that or we'll have to just finish the job," Trump said at a White House cabinet meeting, claiming Iran was "negotiating on fumes." He insisted the midterm elections would not pressure him into accepting unfavorable terms.

Trump also appeared to direct a warning at Oman, a U.S. ally, when discussing proposals for Iran and Oman to jointly manage the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said the strait would be "open to everybody" and "Oman will behave just like everybody else or we'll have to blow them up." The White House did not immediately clarify his remarks.

Iran's state television claimed to possess an unofficial draft agreement that would restore commercial shipping through the strait within a month, with Iran and Oman managing traffic. The White House dismissed this as a "complete fabrication."

A significant unresolved issue concerns whether any U.S.-Iran ceasefire will cover Israeli operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran has insisted Lebanon must be included in ceasefire agreements. Netanyahu said his military is "deepening its operation" in Lebanon, with Israeli forces clashing with Hezbollah fighters and striking over 550 targets this week alone.

The price spike reflects market concerns about potential disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East. Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil passes. For oil-dependent economies worldwide, prices will likely remain elevated until military exchanges cease or diplomatic efforts successfully de-escalate tensions.

cards.headline: Millions of student loan borrowers to need new repayment plan as SAVE program ends
cards.teaser: More than 7 million borrowers will soon need to select a new repayment option for their federal student loans.
cards.body:
More than 7 million borrowers will need to find a new repayment option for their federal student loans as the SAVE plan comes to an end. The transition affects a significant portion of federal student loan holders who currently use the program.

Borrowers will need to select alternative repayment plans for their federal loans. The shift creates uncertainty for millions of loan holders who will need to evaluate different repayment structures. Even the new plans borrowers choose could face elimination quickly, adding to the instability in federal student loan repayment options.

cards.headline: Florida attorney general sues OpenAI over AI safety risks
cards.teaser: The lawsuit seeks to hold CEO Sam Altman personally liable for alleged harms from the company's chatbot technology.
cards.body:
Florida's attorney general filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging that the company's artificial intelligence products pose safety risks. The legal action seeks to hold CEO Sam Altman personally liable for alleged harms connected to the chatbot technology.

The lawsuit centers on concerns that OpenAI's systems are unsafe for children to use. Florida joins a growing number of state officials raising questions about AI safety and the responsibility of companies developing the technology. The case could set precedents for how AI developers are held accountable for their products' impacts.

cards.headline: Anthropic plans to list shares on U.S. stock market
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company behind Claude will offer public shares sometime this year.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the U.S. stock market. The filing comes as the AI industry sees increased investor interest, with the company joining other major tech firms expected to go public this year.

Anthropic recently raised $65 billion in funding, valuing the company at $965 billion. The startup has grown rapidly, becoming popular with software engineers and business clients who use Claude for various tasks.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes off Massachusetts coast with force of 300 tons of TNT
cards.teaser: A meteor entering the atmosphere over Massachusetts prompted reports of loud booms across the United States and Canada.
cards.body:
A meteor roughly 3 feet wide exploded over northeastern Massachusetts near the New Hampshire border on Saturday afternoon, producing a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour. The explosion generated loud booms that echoed across the region.

Reports of the event came from across a wide area, with people from Delaware to Montreal reporting either hearing the booms or witnessing the fireball streaking through the sky. NASA confirmed the incident and indicated that meteorite fragments may be recoverable in the surrounding area.

cards.headline: SpaceX warns prospective investors of potential major equity dilution
cards.teaser: The space company added a disclosure that it may issue significant equity in future transactions after going public.
cards.body:
SpaceX has warned prospective investors that a major dilution could occur after the company completes its initial public offering. The company added the warning as part of its disclosures to potential investors considering purchasing shares.

The disclosure indicates that SpaceX may issue substantial additional equity in future transactions, which would reduce the ownership percentage of existing shareholders. Such warnings are typically included when companies anticipate needing to raise additional capital or use stock for acquisitions or employee compensation after going public.

cards.headline: Nvidia launches chip bringing AI capabilities to personal computers
cards.teaser: The graphics chip maker unveiled new processor technology designed to run AI applications directly on laptops and desktop computers.
cards.body:
Nvidia has launched a new "superchip" called the RTX Spark PC, designed to bring AI processing power directly to laptops and desktop computers running Microsoft Windows. The move represents the semiconductor giant's entry into the PC processor market, where it will compete against Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD.

The chip is intended to run AI applications locally on devices rather than relying on cloud computing. Nvidia suggests the technology could fundamentally change how people interact with computers, potentially replacing traditional input methods like the mouse and keyboard with AI agents.

hero.headline: Ethiopian election suspended in some areas over security concerns
hero.teaser: Voting was halted in parts of Ethiopia as the country holds elections during a period of internal conflict and regional tensions.
hero.body:
Voting has been suspended in certain areas of Ethiopia during the country's national elections. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party is expected to dominate the results.

The suspension reflects ongoing conflicts that are overshadowing the electoral process across the country.

cards.headline: Former Syrian officers face war crimes trial in Austria
cards.teaser: Two Assad regime officials living in Austria will stand trial on torture charges in the country's first prosecution of Syrian government officials.
cards.body:
Austria is conducting its first war crimes trial against Assad regime officials. Two former Syrian officers, who had been living in Austria, face charges of torture. The proceedings will allow Syrian witnesses to directly confront the accused men in court.

This trial represents a significant legal effort to hold Syrian government officials accountable for alleged abuses committed during the country's civil war.

cards.headline: Alberta to hold vote on whether to pursue separation from Canada
cards.teaser: Albertans will vote in October on whether to stay in Canada or hold a referendum on leaving the country.
cards.body:
Alberta will hold a vote in October allowing residents to decide whether the province should remain part of Canada or proceed with a referendum on separation. The vote comes as Alberta's independence movement gains political traction in the province.

The October vote will ask Albertans whether they want to stay in Canada or move forward with holding a formal referendum to leave. The outcome could either resolve longstanding tensions between Alberta and the federal government or deepen the existing divide over the province's place in the country.

cards.headline: UK government releases additional files on former diplomat Peter Mandelson
cards.teaser: Britain released over a thousand pages of documents related to Peter Mandelson, who was dismissed over his connections to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
The UK government released more than a thousand pages of documents related to Peter Mandelson, a former diplomat who was fired due to his links to Jeffrey Epstein. The files included a letter in which Mandelson made claims about needing a complete revamp of the Prime Minister's office and criticized Keir Starmer's leadership.

The release of the documents brings renewed attention to Mandelson's time in government and his connections to Epstein. The files provide additional details about internal communications and assessments made by Mandelson during his tenure.

cards.headline: Britain bars entry to social media personalities Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur
cards.teaser: UK authorities denied entry to two popular online commentators, stating their presence may not be conducive to the public good.
cards.body:
The UK Home Office has denied entry to American left-wing commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker, citing that their presence may not be conducive to the public good. The two content creators, who have substantial online followings, were scheduled to speak at the SXSW London festival and at an event in Oxford.

The Home Office did not provide specific reasons for the decision to bar the US citizens from entering the country.

cards.headline: Singer Dua Lipa marries actor Callum Turner in London
cards.teaser: The couple wed at Old Marylebone Town Hall, a historic venue that has hosted celebrity weddings for decades.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner married at Old Marylebone Town Hall in London. The venue is among the busiest wedding locations in Britain and has a long history of hosting high-profile ceremonies.

Previous celebrity couples who married at the same location include Sylvester Stallone, Paul McCartney, and Lena Dunham. Old Marylebone Town Hall has become a popular choice for prominent figures seeking to marry in London.

cards.headline: Iran warns Israeli strikes in Lebanon could derail US ceasefire efforts
cards.teaser: Iranian officials said Israeli
cards.body:
Israel's Prime Minister ordered military strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs following rocket and drone attacks from Hezbollah on northern Israel.

Iran has warned that Israeli attacks in Lebanon pose a threat to ceasefire efforts between the US and Iran. The strikes come amid ongoing tensions in the region between Israeli forces and the Iran-backed militant group.

hero.headline: Colorado governor commutes sentence of elections clerk imprisoned for security breach
hero.teaser: Tina Peters, a former county clerk convicted of election security crimes, was released from prison after the governor reduced her sentence.
hero.body:
Colorado Governor Jared Polis commuted the sentence of Tina Peters, the former Mesa County elections clerk convicted in connection with a scheme linked to election conspiracy theories. Peters, 70, was released from prison on Monday after serving less than a quarter of her nine-year sentence.

Peters had become a prominent figure among those promoting election denial narratives following the 2020 election. Her release followed pressure from the president to commute her sentence.

cards.headline: AI company Anthropic plans stock market listing
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence firm behind the Claude AI assistant announced it will offer shares to the public later this year.
cards.body:
Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The filing comes as the AI firm experiences rapid growth, with its valuation reaching $965 billion following a recent $65 billion funding round—up from $380 billion just months earlier.

The company joins other major technology firms in pursuing public investment. Anthropic has become a significant player in the competitive AI assistant market, gaining particular traction among software engineers and business clients.

cards.headline: Judge orders public hearings in Charlie Kirk murder case
cards.teaser: A court rejected defense requests to close proceedings in the case against Tyler Robinson, accused of killing Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
A judge ruled that an upcoming hearing for Tyler Robinson, the man charged with murdering Charlie Kirk, will be open to reporters and members of the public. The defense had sought to close the proceedings, but the court denied the request.

Robinson had also requested another delay to allow time for the Supreme Court to consider the issue of cameras in courtrooms. The judge's decision means the hearing will proceed with public and media access. Robinson faces charges in connection with Kirk's death, though trial proceedings are ongoing.

cards.headline: Iowa Democrat criticizes Schumer in Senate primary race
cards.teaser: A Democratic Senate candidate in Iowa is running against Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer as part of campaign strategy ahead of the primary election.
cards.body:
A Democratic candidate in Iowa's Senate primary is testing whether attacking Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer will resonate with voters. The strategy comes as candidates make their final appeals ahead of the primary election on Tuesday.

One candidate, Carlin, criticized Representative Ashley Hinson's vote supporting federal same-sex marriage protections. The primary race has also highlighted farmer frustrations with Trump administration policies, which some analysts suggest could create challenges for Iowa Republicans. Multiple candidates held events across the state as voting approached.

cards.headline: U.K. denies entry to American political commentators
cards.teaser: The British Home Office blocked left-wing content creators Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur from entering the country for scheduled speaking events.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom's Home Office has denied entry to American political commentators Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur. Both are left-wing content creators with large online followings who were scheduled to speak at the SXSW London festival and Oxford University this week.

The US citizens were prevented from participating in their planned appearances, though the Home Office did not publicly state its reasons for the denial.

cards.headline: Former England soccer captain Kevin Keegan diagnosed with stage four cancer
cards.teaser: Kevin Keegan, who captained and later managed England's national soccer team, disclosed he has advanced cancer.
cards.body:
Kevin Keegan, the former England captain and manager, has revealed he has been diagnosed with stage four cancer. The 75-year-old made the announcement during an appearance at the Tyne Theatre and Opera House, sharing that his family had initially disclosed his cancer diagnosis in January.

Keegan said he is working with a specialist doctor who is employing a new treatment approach for his condition. He expressed confidence in his medical team's expertise. Newcastle United sent their "heartfelt support and warmest wishes" following the public announcement of his diagnosis.

cards.headline: Killer sentenced to prison for murder of Southampton university student
cards.teaser: A court jailed a weapons-obsessed individual for killing Henry Nowak as the student walked home from a night out.
cards.body: A court sentenced

The lawsuit centers on concerns that OpenAI's systems are unsafe for children to use. Florida joins a growing number of state officials raising questions about AI safety and the responsibility of companies developing the technology. The case could set precedents for how AI developers are held accountable for their products' impacts.

cards.headline: Barry Diller's People Inc. offers to buy MGM Resorts for $18 billion
cards.teaser: The media mogul's company is preparing to acquire the portion of the casino giant it does not already own.
cards.body:
People Inc., chaired by media mogul Barry Diller, has proposed acquiring MGM Resorts at a valuation exceeding $18 billion. The offer would give People Inc. full ownership of the casino operator.

Diller recently told shareholders that People would focus on its MGM stake, describing the stock as "wildly undervalued." The takeover proposal marks a significant shift for Diller's digital media company into the casino and hospitality sector during volatile market conditions.

cards.body:

cards.headline: United Airlines flight returns to U.S. after Bluetooth device named with profanity
cards.teaser: A passenger labeled a Bluetooth device with a profane word, prompting the flight to Spain to turn around.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Spain returned to Newark Airport after a passenger named a Bluetooth device with a profanity-laden label. The crew identified the device name as a potential security concern and decided to turn the aircraft around while flying over the Atlantic Ocean.

Upon landing, passengers underwent additional security screening. While the incident caused delays, no injuries or property damage occurred. The airline's response reflects standard protocol for treating any flagged security matter seriously, regardless of whether it poses actual danger.

cards.headline: 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley criticizes CBS News leadership in staff meeting
cards.teaser: Pelley attacked CBS editor in chief Bari Weiss and the show's new executive producer Nick Bilton.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent, sharply criticized CBS News leadership during a staff meeting Monday, attacking decisions made by the network's editor-in-chief Bari Weiss. Pelley's comments came after CBS fired the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents—Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega—as part of a broader overhaul.

The heated confrontation occurred during a meeting with staff, newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton, and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle. Pelley's rebuke highlighted mounting tensions at CBS News as the network implements significant changes to the long-running program.

cards.headline: UK banks offered access to OpenAI cyber tool after Anthropic blocks Mythos
cards.teaser: Nine banks received an offer to use GPT 5.5 Cyber as rival Anthropic restricted previews of its own system.
cards.body:
Nine UK banks have been offered access to OpenAI's GPT 5.5 Cyber tool following Anthropic's decision to block their previews of its competing Mythos cybersecurity system. The move gives OpenAI an opportunity to establish itself in the financial services cybersecurity market.

Financial institutions are increasingly investing in artificial intelligence tools to strengthen their defenses against sophisticated cyberattacks. Anthropic's restriction on Mythos access has created an opening for OpenAI to provide banks with an alternative solution for detecting and preventing cyber threats.

hero.headline: Anthropic files confidentially for public offering
hero.body:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, has filed confidentially for an initial public offering on the US stock market, the company announced Monday. The confidential filing marks a significant milestone in the AI startup's path toward becoming a publicly traded company.

The company did not disclose its target valuation for the stock market or other specific terms of the offering. However, Anthropic recently announced a major funding round that valued the company at $965 billion post-money, following a $65 billion investment. This valuation represents a substantial increase from February, when the company was valued at $380 billion.

The confidential filing process allows Anthropic to begin its IPO journey while keeping financial details private until closer to the actual offering. Under securities regulations, companies can file confidentially and later make their prospectus public, typically a few weeks before starting their roadshow to market shares to investors. This approach has become increasingly common among technology companies.

Founded by former OpenAI executives including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic has positioned itself as a research-focused AI company emphasizing safety and responsible development. The Claude AI assistant has become popular with software engineers and other business clients, competing directly with ChatGPT and other large language models in both consumer and enterprise markets.

The company has developed what it calls a constitutional AI approach, which aims to build AI systems with built-in ethical guidelines and safety constraints. Anthropic has raised billions of dollars in private funding from major investors including Google and Salesforce.

The timing of the filing comes as the financial stakes of the AI industry continue to rise. Anthropic's IPO would make it the world's most valuable AI startup, eclipsing its competitor OpenAI, which is expected to file for a public offering in the coming weeks. The AI race has intensified with multiple major players preparing to go public this year.

Elon Musk's SpaceX has also filed for a stock market float at a valuation of about $1.75 trillion while seeking $75 billion in investment. The convergence of these major offerings reflects the significant investor interest in artificial intelligence and space technology sectors.

The confidential filing positions Anthropic to join the public markets at a time when investor interest in artificial intelligence companies remains elevated. Many AI companies have seen their valuations rise substantially over the past two years as businesses across industries adopt AI tools. A successful IPO would give public market investors direct access to one of the leading independent AI companies, separate from the AI divisions embedded within larger technology corporations.

cards.headline: Former Meta CTO raises $250 million climate technology fund
cards.teaser: Mike Schroepfer's Gigascale Capital closed a large fund to back founders building solutions for energy and material shortages.
cards.body:
Mike Schroepfer, Meta's former chief technology officer, has closed a $250 million fund through Gigascale Capital. The fund will invest in founders developing climate-friendly solutions to address global energy and material shortages.

The fundraising move stands out as climate technology investment has cooled among many venture investors. Gigascale Capital is positioning itself to back companies building technologies that tackle carbon emissions and resource constraints.

cards.headline: AI weather startup outperforms government forecasting agencies
cards.teaser: Windborne Systems' newest weather forecasting model beats the best government predictions by days, according to the company.
cards.body:
Windborne Systems has developed a weather forecasting model that the company says outperforms government agency predictions by several days. The artificial intelligence-based system represents a private sector challenge to traditional meteorological forecasting methods.

Weather forecasting has traditionally been dominated by government agencies like the National Weather Service and their international counterparts. Windborne Systems is among a new generation of startups applying machine learning and AI techniques to atmospheric prediction, aiming to provide more accurate or longer-range forecasts than existing public systems.

cards.headline: AMD extends processor socket support through 2029
cards.teaser: The chipmaker announced it will support its Socket AM5 platform through at least 2029, while continuing AM4 production.
cards.body:
AMD announced it will extend support for its Socket AM5 processor platform through at least 2029. The company also continues to support its older AM4 socket, which has remained in production longer than initially expected.

AMD is bringing back the 5800X3D processor at $349 while introducing a new 7700X3D model at $329. Extended socket support allows consumers to upgrade processors without replacing motherboards, a strategy AMD has used to differentiate itself from competitors. The AM4 platform's longevity has been notable in an industry where platforms typically have shorter lifespans.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame receiver Raymond Berry dies at 93
hero.body:
Raymond Berry, a Pro Football Hall of Fame receiver who starred for the Baltimore Colts and later coached the New England Patriots to a Super Bowl victory, has died at age 93.

Berry played 13 seasons in the NFL, all with the Colts, leading the league in receptions three times during his career. He was known for his precise route running and sure hands, becoming one of quarterback Johnny Unitas's favorite targets during Baltimore's championship era. Berry's performance in the 1958 NFL Championship Game, often called the greatest game ever played, helped establish the NFL as a major American sport. He caught 12 passes for 178 yards in that overtime victory against the New York Giants.

After retiring as a player, Berry transitioned to coaching. He served as head coach of the New England Patriots from 1984 to 1989, leading the team to Super Bowl XX following the 1985 season. Though the Patriots lost that game to the Chicago Bears, Berry's coaching tenure marked an important period in the franchise's development. He finished his coaching career with a 51-41 regular season record.

Berry was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1973, recognition of his impact on the game during an era when passing attacks were becoming central to NFL offenses. He finished his playing career with 631 receptions for 9,275 yards and 68 touchdowns. His partnership with Unitas formed one of the most successful quarterback-receiver combinations in NFL history.

Berry's methodical approach to the game, including his attention to detail in preparation and execution, influenced generations of receivers who followed. He was known for running precise routes and studying defensive tendencies, traits that became standard for elite receivers. His contributions to professional football extended across multiple decades as both a player and coach.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams in blockbuster deal
cards.teaser: Cleveland is sending its star defensive end to Los Angeles in exchange for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick and additional draft compensation.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns are trading defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams, according to ESPN sources. In return, the Browns will receive linebacker Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round draft pick, and additional draft compensation.

Garrett, selected first overall by Cleveland in 2017, has established himself as one of the NFL's elite pass rushers. The trade marks a major shift for the Browns' roster while strengthening the Rams' defensive line.

cards.headline: Giants sign Odell Beckham Jr. to bolster receiving corps
cards.teaser: The wide receiver returns to New York, where he began his NFL career and earned three Pro Bowl selections.
cards.body:
The New York Giants have signed wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr., the team announced. Beckham returns to the franchise that drafted him in 2014, where he spent his first five NFL seasons before being traded to Cleveland.

Beckham made three Pro Bowl appearances during his initial tenure with the Giants and became known for spectacular catches and explosive playmaking ability. The signing adds an experienced receiver to New York's offensive unit.

cards.headline: Serena Williams to return to professional tennis at 44
cards.teaser: The 23-time Grand Slam champion will play doubles at next week's HSBC Championships in London after nearly four years away from competition.
cards.body:
Serena Williams is returning to professional tennis at age 44, nearly four years after stepping away from the sport following the 2022 US Open. She will compete in the women's doubles at Queen's Club in London next week as a wildcard entry.

Williams will partner with Victoria Mboko in the WTA 500 event. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion has described her departure from tennis as "evolving away" from the sport rather than a retirement, though she remained on the retired players' list until recently.

cards.headline: Russell Wilson leaving NFL to join CBS Sports as analyst
cards.teaser: The veteran quarterback is finalizing a deal to transition from playing to broadcasting.
cards.body:
Quarterback Russell Wilson is finalizing a deal to become a CBS Sports analyst, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The move marks the end of Wilson's playing career as he transitions into broadcasting.

Wilson spent most of his NFL career with the Seattle Seahawks, where he led the team to two Super Bowl appearances and won one championship. He later played for the Denver Broncos before his most recent stint with another NFL team.

cards.headline: French Open fines player $76,000 for sexist remark about umpire
cards.teaser: Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo must pay half his prize money after saying his match should not have been umpired by a woman.
cards.body:
Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo has been fined approximately $76,000 by the French Open for making a sexist comment about his match umpire. The penalty amounts to half of his tournament prize money.

Vallejo objected to having a woman umpire his second-round match. The fine represents a significant penalty for conduct violations at a Grand Slam tournament, underscoring the sport's commitment to maintaining professional standards among players.

cards.headline: Illinois delays Bears stadium vote until fall session
cards.teaser: State lawmakers adjourned without passing legislation aimed at keeping the franchise in Illinois, with the team set to announce its decision soon.
cards.body:
Illinois lawmakers have adjourned their spring session without voting on legislation aimed at keeping the Chicago Bears in the state. The stadium funding proposal will now be addressed during the fall session.

The Bears have indicated they plan to announce their decision about their future home in the coming weeks, leaving the timing uncertain as the legislature postpones action on the bill.

hero.headline: Florida Sues OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman Over User Safety Claims
hero.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed an 83-page lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in Florida circuit court, alleging the company prioritized profits over user safety. The complaint accuses the company's rise as being backed by a web of deception and the exploitation of users, including Florida residents.

The legal action marks a significant escalation in state-level scrutiny of artificial intelligence companies and their leadership. The lawsuit targets both the company and Altman personally, seeking to hold them accountable for alleged harm to users. Florida's complaint asserts that OpenAI leveraged user data and trust while failing to adequately protect those interacting with its technology.

The timing of the lawsuit comes as artificial intelligence companies face increasing pressure from regulators and lawmakers over safety concerns, data privacy, and the potential risks posed by rapidly advancing AI systems. OpenAI, which operates ChatGPT and other AI tools used by millions globally, has been at the center of debates about how to balance innovation with responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence.

The 83-page filing represents one of the most detailed legal challenges against OpenAI to date from a state government. Attorney General Uthmeier's complaint focuses on the company's alleged exploitation of Florida users and what the state characterizes as deceptive practices during OpenAI's growth.

This lawsuit against Altman and OpenAI comes amid broader scrutiny of the CEO's conduct and character. In recent legal proceedings, Altman has faced accusations from former colleagues regarding his trustworthiness. During testimony in another case, Musk's attorneys presented statements from former OpenAI executives suggesting Altman had misled them or misrepresented himself. These challenges to his credibility highlight ongoing concerns about leadership practices within the company.

The complaint does not specify the exact nature of the alleged risks to human life or detail specific incidents involving Florida residents.

OpenAI has not publicly responded to the lawsuit. The case could have broader implications for how states regulate AI companies and whether executives can be held personally liable for corporate decisions related to emerging technologies. The outcome may influence other states considering similar legal action against technology companies over safety and consumer protection concerns.

The lawsuit adds to the mounting legal challenges facing OpenAI and Altman. The company has faced various regulatory pressures and legal disputes as artificial intelligence technology becomes increasingly prominent in everyday applications. How this case develops could set important precedents for state-level regulation of AI companies and the personal accountability of their leadership.

cards.headline: Anna Kendrick to Direct Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo for Netflix
cards.teaser: The actress joins the adaptation of Taylor Jenkins Reid's bestselling novel after two previous directors departed the project.
cards.body:
Anna Kendrick has been hired to direct The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo for Netflix, becoming the third filmmaker attached to the project. Maggie Betts and Leslye Headland previously left the adaptation for reasons that have not been disclosed.

The film adapts Taylor Jenkins Reid's 2017 bestselling novel, which follows a fictional Old Hollywood star. Kendrick takes over the project after the departures of both previous directors, though Netflix is moving forward with the high-profile book adaptation.

cards.headline: CBS News Works to Keep Scott Pelley at 60 Minutes After Clash With New Boss
cards.teaser: The veteran correspondent met with the show's new head after reports of a heated confrontation.
cards.body:
CBS News hopes to retain Scott Pelley at 60 Minutes following a heated confrontation during a staff meeting on Monday. Pelley, a veteran correspondent, strongly criticized the network's recent decision to fire the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

The clash occurred during a meeting with Nick Bilton, the newly appointed executive producer, and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle. Pelley directly attacked Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief, over the layoffs as part of the show's broader overhaul.

cards.headline: Superman Sequel Reveals Lex Luthor's Warsuit
cards.teaser: Director James Gunn shared the first look at Nicholas Hoult in the villain's iconic armor from the set of Man of Tomorrow.
cards.body:
Director James Gunn revealed the first look at Lex Luthor's warsuit from the set of Man of Tomorrow, the sequel to Superman. Nicholas Hoult appears in the villain's iconic armor as production continues on the film.

Gunn posted the image with the caption "Fit check. Live from the set of Man of Tomorrow." The warsuit represents one of Lex Luthor's most recognizable weapons from the comics, marking a significant escalation in the character's confrontation with Superman in the sequel.

cards.headline: Streets of Rage Movie Lands Sonic Writers and Director
cards.teaser: Lionsgate has tapped Sonic the Hedgehog franchise writers Pat Casey and Josh Miller for the video game adaptation.
cards.body:
Pat Casey and Josh Miller, the writers behind Paramount's Sonic the Hedgehog film franchise, will write the adaptation of Sega's Streets of Rage video game for Lionsgate. Jeymes Samuel, who directed The Harder They Fall, has joined the project as director.

The film brings together talent from successful video game adaptations and acclaimed independent cinema. Casey and Miller have been credited with the success of the Sonic films, while Samuel's previous work demonstrated his visual style and storytelling abilities.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Contestant Before Season Premiere Over Alleged Slur
cards.teaser: The reality show dismissed a cast member from Salem ahead of the eighth season after videos surfaced.
cards.body:
Love Island USA removed a contestant from its eighth season cast before the premiere after videos surfaced showing the person using a racial slur. The dismissed cast member operated a salon in Salem.

The show took action after the videos circulated online. The contestant will not appear in the upcoming season, which was set to begin shortly.

cards.headline: Julia Roberts and Lily Gladstone Join First Amendment Concert Lineup
cards.teaser: The actresses will participate in a June concert organized by Jane Fonda's Committee for the First Amendment.
cards.body:
Julia Roberts, Lily Gladstone, Wilson Cruz, and Peppermint will participate in Rise Up, Sing Out: A Concert for the First Amendment next month. The event is organized by the Jane Fonda-led Committee for the First Amendment.

The quartet joins a lineup that includes Jane Fonda, Bette Midler, Patti Smith, Joy Reid, and Rufus Wainwright. The concert aims to support First Amendment rights and freedoms.

hero.headline: Trump and Johnson meet over Justice Department fund as Republicans voice concerns
hero.body:
President Trump met with Speaker Mike Johnson at the White House to discuss the Justice Department's $1.776 billion anti-weaponization fund. Sources in the Speaker's office confirmed the meeting took place as Republican lawmakers in both chambers have expressed frustration over the fund.

The fund has become a point of contention among Republicans in Congress. Lawmakers from the House and Senate have raised concerns about the allocation and purpose of the $1.776 billion designated for what the administration calls anti-weaponization efforts within the Justice Department.

The meeting between Trump and Johnson signals an attempt to address internal party tensions over the controversial funding. The anti-weaponization fund represents a significant portion of Justice Department resources, and its creation has sparked debate about departmental priorities and spending oversight.

Sources from Johnson's office confirmed the discussion to multiple news outlets, including The Hill and NewsNation. The Speaker's involvement suggests Republican leadership is working to resolve disagreements within the party over the fund's structure and implementation.

The tension over the fund adds to broader debates about Justice Department operations and priorities under the Trump administration. Republican concerns about the allocation highlight divisions within the party over how federal law enforcement resources should be directed and managed. The outcome of the White House meeting could shape how Congress approaches oversight and funding decisions for the Justice Department in coming months.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Park Service from revoking permit for anti-Trump protest over flag
cards.teaser: A federal judge temporarily stopped the National Park Service from ending a 24/7 protest permit in Washington over the display of an 86 47 flag.
cards.body:
A federal judge temporarily blocked the National Park Service from revoking a permit for a continuous anti-Trump protest in Washington, D.C. on Monday. The agency had sought to end the permit after protesters displayed an "86 47" flag at the demonstration site.

The Secret Service flagged the statement on the flag as a potential call for violence against the president, and federal officers ordered its removal. The judge's ruling allows the protest to continue while the permit dispute proceeds through the courts.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran suspension of talks is fine with him
cards.teaser: President Trump said he was unaware Iran suspended negotiations with the United States over Israeli military actions in Lebanon.
cards.body:
President Trump said he was unaware that Iran had suspended talks with the United States over Israeli military actions in Lebanon. When informed of the decision, Trump appeared unconcerned, telling reporters that if Iran doesn't want to negotiate, he is comfortable with that outcome.

Trump's dismissal of the suspended talks contrasts with reports that he has been actively seeking a deal to end the conflict before it damages the global economy and affects Republican prospects in upcoming elections. According to analysts, Iran currently holds a stronger negotiating position than before, yet Trump has struggled to advance diplomatic efforts effectively.

cards.headline: Florida becomes first state to sue OpenAI over product design claims
cards.teaser: Florida's attorney general filed suit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging they promoted a product they knew could harm users.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, making Florida the first state to pursue legal action against the AI company over product design. The complaint alleges that OpenAI promoted its products, including ChatGPT, while knowing they could harm users.

The case represents a new wave of state-level legal challenges targeting artificial intelligence firms. The outcome could establish important precedent for how states regulate AI companies and hold them responsible for their design decisions.

cards.headline: Republican lawmaker says Iran deal could take very long time to complete
cards.teaser: Rep. Darrell Issa said securing a deal to end the war in Iran could require extensive negotiations despite a ceasefire being in place.
cards.body:
Rep. Darrell Issa said Sunday that securing a deal to end the war with Iran could take considerable time. The California Republican made the comments during an appearance on Fox News's "The Sunday Briefing," when host Peter Doocy asked about the timeline for resolving the conflict.

Issa's assessment suggests lengthy negotiations lie ahead, even as a ceasefire currently pauses active fighting. His remarks underscore the challenges both sides face in reaching a final agreement to end the conflict.

cards.headline: Former North Carolina officer charged after video shows woman punched during arrest
cards.teaser: Karson Hyder, fired from the Shelby Police Department, faces charges after doorbell camera footage showed him allegedly punching a woman.
cards.body:
Karson Hyder, a former Shelby, North Carolina, police officer, has been charged after video captured on a Ring doorbell camera showed him allegedly punching a woman during an arrest. Hyder was fired from the police department following the incident.

The doorbell camera footage surfaced showing the alleged assault during the arrest. The charges come after Hyder's termination from the Shelby Police Department. The case highlights the role of home surveillance technology in documenting police conduct during arrests.

cards.headline: Millions of student loan borrowers to need new repayment plan as SAVE program ends
cards.teaser: More than 7 million borrowers will soon need to select a new repayment option for their federal student loans.
cards.body:
More than 7 million borrowers will need to find a new repayment option for their federal student loans as the SAVE plan comes to an end. The transition affects a significant portion of federal student loan holders who currently use the program.

Borrowers will need to select alternative repayment plans for their federal loans. The shift creates uncertainty for millions of loan holders who will need to evaluate different repayment structures. Even the new plans borrowers choose could face elimination quickly, adding to the instability in federal student loan repayment options.
